Keywords: Disclosed, The

outputs.L1: The present invention discloses a method and apparatus for antenna management. The method comprises: collecting resource usage status data from managed access networks; selecting, from the managed access networks according to the resource usage status data, access networks participating in antenna scheduling to form an antenna scheduling set, wherein access networks using the same spectrum resources are included in the same antenna scheduling set; dividing radio links of each access network in the antenna scheduling set into one or more radio link clusters; allocating radio resources to each radio link cluster in the antenna scheduling set such that mutual interference among all radio link clusters in the antenna scheduling set is maintained within a preset range; and sending radio resource allocation results to the access networks to which the radio link clusters belong. The method and apparatus enable as many access networks as possible to operate simultaneously within an allowable interference range while using the same spectrum resources, thereby increasing spectrum multiplexing opportunities and achieving a high resource utilization rate.
outputs.L2:
The invention describes a technique and device for managing antennas. In this approach, information about resource usage is obtained from the access networks under management. Based on that information, the access networks involved in antenna scheduling are chosen from the managed access networks to form an antenna scheduling group. Access networks that use identical spectrum resources are placed into the same scheduling group.

Within each access network included in the antenna scheduling group, radio links are separated into one or more radio link clusters. Radio resources are then assigned to each radio link cluster in the group so that interference between the clusters remains within a predefined allowable range. The results of the radio resource assignment are subsequently transmitted to the access networks to which the corresponding radio link clusters belong.

This method and apparatus allow the largest possible number of access networks to operate simultaneously on the same spectrum resource while keeping interference within permitted limits. As a result, opportunities for spectrum reuse are increased, and overall resource utilization efficiency is improved.
outputs.L3:
The invention discloses a method and apparatus for antenna management, particularly for coordinating the use of antenna and radio resources among multiple managed access networks. The solution is designed to improve spectrum utilization while controlling interference between radio links that may operate in overlapping or identical spectrum resources.

According to the method, resource use status data are first collected from a plurality of managed access networks. The resource use status data may include information such as spectrum occupancy, radio link activity, channel usage, interference levels, traffic load, and other parameters reflecting the current or predicted use of radio resources in each access network. Based on this information, one or more access networks are selected for antenna scheduling.

Access networks that use the same spectrum resources are then grouped into the same antenna scheduling set. By placing access networks sharing identical or overlapping spectrum resources into a common scheduling set, the method enables coordinated management of radio transmissions among those networks. This helps prevent uncontrolled interference and allows the system to make more efficient scheduling decisions across multiple networks.

For each access network included in an antenna scheduling set, the radio links are further divided into one or more radio link clusters. A radio link cluster may include radio links that have similar interference characteristics, geographical proximity, traffic requirements, channel conditions, or other relevant attributes. Clustering the radio links allows the system to manage radio resources at a more granular level rather than treating the entire access network as a single scheduling unit.

Radio resources are then allocated to the radio link clusters according to the antenna scheduling result. The allocation may include assigning frequency resources, time resources, spatial resources, beam directions, antenna elements, transmission power, or combinations thereof. The allocation is performed so that mutual interference among the clusters, and among the access networks in the same scheduling set, remains within a preset range or threshold.

By controlling interference in this manner, the invention enables multiple radio links and access networks to reuse the same or overlapping spectrum resources more effectively. As a result, the method and apparatus can increase spectrum reuse, improve overall radio resource utilization, enhance network capacity, and maintain reliable communication performance across the managed access networks.
outputs.L4:
A method and apparatus for antenna management are provided for coordinating the use of radio resources among multiple access networks operating in the same or overlapping frequency spectrum. The method includes collecting resource-use information from a plurality of access networks, such as information identifying active antennas, assigned frequencies, time slots, transmission powers, beam directions, radio links, traffic loads, and interference conditions. The collected information may be received from base stations, access points, network controllers, user devices, spectrum management entities, or other network elements capable of reporting current or anticipated use of radio resources.

Based on the collected information, access networks that use the same spectrum, or spectrum portions that may interfere with one another, are grouped into one or more antenna scheduling sets. Each antenna scheduling set includes networks, antennas, or radio links whose transmissions should be coordinated because simultaneous operation may create mutual interference. Within each scheduling set, the radio links associated with the antennas are further organized into clusters. The clustering may be based on geographic proximity, signal strength, antenna orientation, beam overlap, propagation characteristics, interference measurements, quality-of-service requirements, or other criteria that indicate whether one radio link may affect another.

After the radio links have been clustered, the apparatus allocates radio resources among the clustered links. The allocation may include assigning frequencies, time periods, transmission opportunities, spatial beams, transmit power levels, coding and modulation schemes, or other controllable radio parameters. The allocation is performed so that links likely to interfere with one another are separated, power-limited, beam-steered, or otherwise coordinated, while links that can coexist without excessive interference are allowed to operate simultaneously. In this manner, the system manages antenna operation across multiple access networks rather than treating each network independently.

The apparatus may include one or more processors, memory, communication interfaces, and control logic configured to perform the collection, grouping, clustering, and allocation functions. The apparatus may be implemented in a centralized spectrum controller, a distributed radio resource management system, an access network controller, a base station, or a cloud-based network management platform. In some implementations, the apparatus continuously or periodically updates its resource allocations in response to changes in traffic demand, network topology, channel conditions, device mobility, or detected interference.

By coordinating antenna scheduling across access networks that share spectrum, the method reduces harmful interference and allows radio resources to be reused more efficiently. More access networks, antennas, or radio links can therefore operate at the same time while maintaining interference within acceptable limits. This increases opportunities for spectrum reuse, improves overall resource utilization, enhances network capacity, and supports more reliable communication in environments where multiple wireless systems compete for limited spectrum.

**Disclosed: The Power of Truth**

Disclosed: the word itself suggests a moment of revelation, when something hidden is finally brought into the open. In everyday life, disclosure can take many forms. It may be a personal truth shared with a close friend, an important fact revealed in a report, or information made public for the benefit of society.

The act of disclosure is often connected to trust. When people are honest about what they know, what they have done, or what they believe, they create space for understanding and accountability. In business, politics, journalism, and relationships, what is disclosed can shape decisions and change outcomes.

However, disclosure also carries responsibility. Not every truth is simple, and not every secret is harmless. The timing, context, and purpose of revealing information matter. When something is disclosed with care, it can lead to clarity and progress. When it is disclosed recklessly, it can create confusion or harm.

In the end, “Disclosed, The” can be understood as the beginning of a story about truth coming to light. It reminds us that what is hidden does not always stay hidden—and that honesty, when handled wisely, has the power to transform situations and people alike.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for an invention about antenna management that schedules multiple access networks using the same spectrum while keeping interference within a preset range.
counterfactuals.output: An antenna management system and method are disclosed for coordinating multiple access networks that operate within a shared spectrum band. The system monitors spectrum use, traffic demand, channel conditions, and interference levels associated with a plurality of antennas and access networks, and dynamically schedules transmission and reception resources among the networks. A controller assigns time, frequency, spatial, beamforming, or power parameters to each access network based on a preset interference range or threshold. When predicted or measured interference exceeds the preset range, the controller modifies scheduling, adjusts antenna patterns, reallocates resources, or changes transmit power to maintain coexistence among the networks. The invention enables concurrent or coordinated operation of heterogeneous access technologies using common spectrum while preserving service quality and limiting harmful interference.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a "Disclosed in the present invention..." style summary describing a method and apparatus for collecting resource use status data, forming antenna scheduling sets, clustering radio links, and allocating radio resources.
counterfactuals.output:
Disclosed in the present invention are a method and apparatus for radio resource allocation. The method comprises: collecting resource use status data associated with a plurality of radio links, the resource use status data including at least one of channel state information, interference information, traffic demand information, beam direction information, antenna availability information, scheduling history, and quality-of-service requirement information; determining, according to the collected resource use status data, a plurality of antenna scheduling sets, each antenna scheduling set including one or more antennas or antenna ports available for scheduling within a scheduling interval; clustering the plurality of radio links based on one or more correlation metrics derived from the resource use status data, the correlation metrics including at least one of spatial correlation, interference correlation, link priority, traffic similarity, and compatibility of antenna scheduling sets; and allocating radio resources to the clustered radio links according to the antenna scheduling sets and clustering results.

In some embodiments, the forming of the antenna scheduling sets comprises identifying antennas capable of serving one or more target radio links, excluding antennas having resource occupancy exceeding a predetermined threshold, and grouping remaining antennas according to beam coverage, interference constraints, or scheduling priority. In some embodiments, the clustering of radio links comprises assigning radio links that may be simultaneously scheduled with acceptable mutual interference to a same cluster, and assigning radio links having conflicting antenna or spectrum requirements to different clusters.

The allocation of radio resources may comprise assigning at least one of time resources, frequency resources, spatial resources, power resources, beam resources, and code resources to each radio link or link cluster. The allocation may be performed so as to maximize system throughput, improve spectrum utilization, satisfy service quality requirements, reduce inter-link interference, balance load among antennas, or a combination thereof.

Also disclosed is an apparatus for implementing the foregoing method. The apparatus comprises: a data collection module configured to obtain resource use status data of radio links and antennas; a scheduling-set forming module configured to generate antenna scheduling sets based on the resource use status data; a clustering module configured to cluster radio links according to link correlation or scheduling compatibility; and a resource allocation module configured to allocate radio resources to the clustered radio links using the antenna scheduling sets. The apparatus may further comprise a storage module configured to store historical scheduling data and a control module configured to update scheduling sets, clustering results, and resource allocation decisions periodically or in response to a change in network status.

By collecting current resource use status data, forming antenna scheduling sets, clustering radio links, and allocating resources based on the scheduling sets and clustering results, the disclosed method and apparatus can improve radio resource utilization, reduce interference among radio links, enhance scheduling efficiency, and support dynamic adaptation to changing network conditions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a telecom patent abstract for an antenna scheduling technique that increases spectrum reuse among managed access networks by grouping networks sharing spectrum resources and controlling mutual interference.
counterfactuals.output: A method and apparatus for antenna scheduling in managed access networks are disclosed. A spectrum management entity identifies a plurality of managed access networks sharing one or more spectrum resources and groups the networks according to geographic proximity, antenna configuration, traffic demand, channel occupancy, or predicted interference coupling. For each group, the entity determines antenna scheduling parameters including beam direction, antenna activation timing, transmit power, polarization, null-steering configuration, or resource block allocation. The scheduling parameters are coordinated among the grouped networks to permit concurrent use of the shared spectrum while maintaining mutual interference below one or more thresholds. Interference measurements or channel state information reported by access points or user equipment may be used to update the grouping and scheduling dynamically. By coordinating directional antenna use and temporal or spatial transmission opportunities among networks, spectrum reuse is increased without requiring exclusive channel assignment, thereby improving aggregate capacity and reliability in shared-spectrum deployments.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: In patent language, describe an invention where managed access networks report resource usage, participating networks are selected into scheduling sets, their radio links are clustered, and resource allocation results are sent back to the networks.
counterfactuals.output:
A method is provided for coordinating radio-resource allocation among a plurality of managed access networks. In one embodiment, each managed access network monitors and reports resource-usage information associated with one or more radio links under its control. The resource-usage information may include, for example, traffic demand, channel quality, interference measurements, bandwidth utilization, scheduling constraints, or quality-of-service requirements.

A coordination entity receives the reported resource-usage information and selects, from among the plurality of managed access networks, one or more participating managed access networks to form a scheduling set. The selection may be based at least in part on the reported resource usage, interference relationships, geographic proximity, service requirements, or available radio resources.

For the selected scheduling set, radio links associated with the participating managed access networks are grouped into one or more clusters. Each cluster may include radio links that are related by interference, shared spectrum usage, traffic characteristics, or scheduling dependency. The coordination entity determines resource-allocation results for the clustered radio links, including allocation of time, frequency, spatial, power, or code resources. The resource-allocation results may be generated so as to reduce interference, improve throughput, satisfy quality-of-service constraints, or balance loading among the participating managed access networks.

The coordination entity then transmits the resource-allocation results to the corresponding participating managed access networks. Each participating managed access network applies the received resource-allocation results to schedule transmissions over its respective radio links. In this manner, radio resources may be coordinated across multiple managed access networks while allowing each network to retain local control over its associated radio links.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an English abstract for a wireless communication patent titled "Method and apparatus for antenna management," emphasizing simultaneous operation of access networks on the same spectrum resource within an allowed interference range.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract**

A method and apparatus for antenna management in a wireless communication system are disclosed. A communication device determines an interference condition associated with simultaneous operation of a plurality of access networks using a same spectrum resource. Based on the determined interference condition, the device controls one or more antenna parameters, including antenna selection, antenna configuration, beam direction, transmission power, reception mode, or scheduling of antenna resources, so that the access networks operate concurrently while interference between the access networks remains within an allowed interference range. The apparatus may monitor signal quality, interference level, traffic demand, or network priority information and dynamically adjust antenna usage to maintain communication performance. Accordingly, multiple access networks can share the same frequency resource at the same time, improving spectrum utilization while satisfying interference constraints.
